newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Aug wholesale inventories rose 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Aug wholesale inventories rose 0.5 pct.

text.p: Commerce Department report of wholesale inventories and sales, seasonally adjusted.
(Billions of dollars) Aug July--Rev from Aug'95
(Billions of dollars) Aug July--Rev from Aug'95
The stock-to-sales ratio for merchant wholesalers, seasonally adjusted, rose to 1.30 months' worth in August from 1.28 months' worth in July.
The ratio is a measure of how many months it would take to sell existing inventories at the current sales pace.

The department said the 0.5 percent increase in August wholesale inventories was the largest rise in four months since a 1.2 percent jump in April 1996. The level of August inventories, at $260.31 billion, was the highest since the series began in 1980, department officials said.
The 0.9 percent drop in August wholesale sales was the largest decline since a 1.0 percent fall in January.
